questions.q: Which two paths can bring a transaction into Receivables?
options: Only manual entry; Receivables cannot import data
Email and fax only
Manual entry and AutoInvoice import
Only AutoInvoice; manual entry was removed in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Transactions are either keyed directly into the Transactions Workbench, or imported and validated through AutoInvoice from an upstream source system.

questions.q: What is the most common date basis used to calculate a due date?
options: The receipt date
The transaction (invoice) date
The customer's credit review date
The general ledger period close date
questions.explain: The transaction date is the most common anchor, though ship date or other system-derived dates can also serve as the date basis.

questions.q: Where would you go to set up a 2% discount for paying within 10 days?
options: Receivables activities
Payment terms
Memo lines
Transaction sources
questions.explain: Payment terms define due dates, installment schedules, and any early-payment discount percentages and periods.

questions.q: What site use, besides Bill-To, is typically assigned alongside it during customer creation?
options: Ship-To
Statements
Dunning
Collector
questions.explain: Ship-To is the other common site use, identifying where goods are delivered; it supports fulfillment and tax determination.

questions.q: Why did Northwind Fixtures Co. set up two separate customer accounts for Harborline Retail Group in the example?
options: Because Harborline is two unrelated parties
Because Oracle Fusion requires one account per party site
Because credit memos require a separate account
Because Harborline's east and west store divisions needed to be invoiced and aged independently, even though both trace to the same party
questions.explain: A single party can have multiple customer accounts when separate business relationships (like independently tracked divisions) need their own terms and aging.

questions.q: Which two scenarios are the main reasons Receivables stores a customer's bank account details?
options: Direct debit / automatic receipts, and electronic refunds
Printing invoices and calculating tax
Assigning a salesperson and setting a credit limit
Creating a transaction type and a memo line
questions.explain: Most receipts simply arrive without needing bank details on file in advance; automatic receipts and refunds are the two cases that do.

questions.q: What does the 'creation sign' on a transaction type control?
options: Which language the invoice prints in
Whether transactions of this type increase or decrease the customer's balance
The customer's credit limit
Whether a receipt can be reversed
questions.explain: Creation sign determines whether a transaction type normally adds to or subtracts from what the customer owes — positive for most invoices, negative for most credit memos.

questions.q: In the Harborline Retail Group maintenance contract example, what happened at the invoice's completion in January?
options: The full $12,000 was booked as a debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Unearned Revenue
$12,000 of revenue was recognized immediately
No accounting entry was created until the contract ended
$1,000 was recognized and the remaining $11,000 was written off
questions.explain: The full invoice amount books to Unearned Revenue at completion; revenue is only recognized incrementally as each month's recognition process runs.

questions.q: Why does consistency matter when using memo lines across a business?
options: So the same type of ad hoc charge (like a restocking fee) always posts to the same account regardless of who enters it or which customer it's billed to
It doesn't matter; each person can account for a charge however they like
Because memo lines are only used once and then deleted
Because tax rates change daily
questions.explain: The whole value of a memo line is that it standardizes how a recurring, ad hoc kind of charge or credit is described and accounted for.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. / Harborline Retail Group example, how was the $12,500 invoice amount calculated?
options: 500 units at $25 each
A flat $12,500 fee
A 50/50 split payment term
An automatic AutoInvoice import
questions.explain: The example invoice line was 500 units of a fixture at $25 per unit, totaling $12,500.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. example, why did 3 of the 400 lines fail validation?
options: They exceeded the customer's credit limit
They used the wrong currency
They were duplicate transactions
They referenced a customer site that had been end-dated
questions.explain: The 3 failing lines referenced an end-dated customer site, which is exactly the kind of line-level issue the validation phase catches.

questions.q: What location does tax determination primarily consider?
options: The bill-to location only, regardless of where goods ship
The ship-to location, along with the item's nature and the customer's exemption status
The business unit's headquarters address
The transaction source
questions.explain: Tax is generally determined based on the ship-to location, the item or service, and whether the customer holds a relevant exemption.

questions.q: What is unapplied cash?
options: Cash that has been refunded to a customer
Money from a known customer that hasn't been matched to a specific transaction yet
A journal entry created during period close
Cash collected through a lockbox that failed validation
questions.explain: Unapplied cash is tied to a known customer but has not yet been applied against any specific open transaction.

questions.q: Which of the following is required for a transaction to be eligible for automatic receipt creation?
options: The transaction must be in a foreign currency
The customer must have no credit limit
The receipt method's receipt class must have a creation method of Automatic
The transaction must be a miscellaneous receipt
questions.explain: Only transactions tied to a receipt method whose receipt class is configured for automatic creation are eligible for the batch.

questions.q: What does 'unapplying' a receipt from a transaction do?
options: Permanently deletes the receipt from the system
Reverses the application, restoring the transaction's balance due and freeing the receipt amount
Automatically writes off the transaction
Converts the receipt into a miscellaneous receipt
questions.explain: Unapplying reverses a receipt application, returning the transaction's balance due and making the receipt amount available to apply elsewhere.

questions.q: What drives the escalation of letters under aged dunning?
options: The time since the last dunning letter was sent
How old the customer's single oldest past-due transaction is
The customer's credit limit
The receipt method assigned to the customer
questions.explain: Aged dunning escalates based on how far past due the customer's oldest open transaction is, rather than the timing of prior letters.

questions.q: What does an aging report 'by common currency' do?
options: Excludes any customer with multiple currencies
Converts every transaction's balance into a single reporting currency so totals can be compared directly
Only reports balances in US dollars regardless of configuration
Removes currency information from the report entirely
questions.explain: Aging by common currency converts balances into one reporting currency, giving a unified total per bucket for companies invoicing in multiple currencies.

questions.q: What does an adjustment do in Oracle Fusion Receivables?
options: Creates a brand-new invoice for the customer
Changes the balance due on a specific transaction directly, without a receipt or credit memo
Automatically reverses a receipt
Merges two customer accounts together
questions.explain: An adjustment is a direct correction tool that changes a transaction's balance due without involving a receipt or a separate credit transaction.

questions.q: What is the typical accounting entry for a standard receipt?
options: Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Revenue
Debit Revenue, credit Cash
Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Cash
Debit Cash, credit Accounts Receivable
questions.explain: A standard receipt is the mirror image of an invoice: it debits Cash and credits Accounts Receivable, reducing what the customer owes.

questions.q: What does the Prepare Receivables to General Ledger Reconciliation process produce?
options: A customer statement for every open account
A dunning letter escalation schedule
A list of all approved write-offs for the year
A report comparing the Receivables-side balance to the GL-side balance by account
questions.explain: This process prepares data for the Receivables to Ledger Reconciliation Report, which lays the Receivables and GL balances side by side by account.

questions.q: What course comes next in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path after Oracle Fusion Accounts Receivable?
options: Oracle Fusion Procure-to-Pay
SQL for Oracle Financials
Oracle Fusion Security
Oracle Fusion Cash Management
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Cash Management is the first course in the Financial Operations stage, which follows directly after the Financials Configuration stage that includes Accounts Receivable.
